Please follow the issue template and provide clear steps to reproduce and example code.

This snippet won't compile since there's no definition for `CardNode`. We shouldn't have to reverse engineer your game to know whether you found an actual bug or not.

This is your third interaction with this issue tracker today, all of which were somewhat unconstructive. I understand that you might be frustrated with a bug in your codebase which you traced back to a potential upstream issue, but a public issue tracker is not the place to rant or throw minimal effort reports with disregard for the project's guidelines.

I removed that var. Now it will compile. Why could you not just remove it yourself? It was just one line, are you serious? You made no effort.

And I'm sorry but your attitude is fucking awful. You are abusing your position of power. It's impossible to bring up an issue without seeing you immediately become defensive and brush it under the rug. You are the true raid boss of this github

I'm not being defensive, I'm just asking you to stay constructive in your bug reports, and do some effort to make them actually actionable by contributors.

Case in point, I tested this one now that you modified the script so it can compile:

[new-game-project2.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/18812910/new-game-project2.zip)

```gdscript
extends Node2D

class Card extends Resource:
	var name: String
	var energy_cost: int
	var attack: int
	var health: int
	func _init(p_name: String = "", p_energy_cost: int = 0, p_attack: int = 0, p_health: int = 0):
		name = p_name
		energy_cost = p_energy_cost
		attack = p_attack
		health = p_health

func _ready():
	var card = Card.new()
	var this_works: Card = card
	var this_crashes_the_program: Card = card.duplicate(true)
	print(this_works)
	print(this_works is Card)
	print(this_crashes_the_program)
	print(this_crashes_the_program is Card)
```

This prints:
```
<Resource#-9223372010531322557>
true
<Resource#-9223372010514545336>
true
```

There's no crash, and the type isn't changed/lost unlike what your issue claims.
So I don't understand what's the bug that you claim is reproduced by this script.

>Why could you not just remove it yourself? It was just one line, are you serious? You made no effort.

If you're not simply trolling, then I highly suggest taking a look in the mirror. I'm surprised that this "bug report" was even entertained because it itself is so low effort. What kind of attitude is this? Where did you get the idea that people should fix your code to even begin triaging the problem? Then you are surprised that Godot has a backlog of issues? Again, take a look at a mirror.

Jesus christ. You people are disturbingly cultish, oh my god.

Thank you for your benevolence, I can see that you come from a kind and well-meaning place. You've set a great example for everyone else that wants to be helpful. Thank you. 

My only suggestion is taking a picture of your monitor with the code instead of copy pasting it directly. Then it would be even more helpful to others.
